componentPlan.focusQuote: On June 11, 1776, the Congress appointed three concurrent committees in response to the Lee Resolution
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Orders dated votes and committee steps to show how independence moved forward in time

componentPlan.focusQuote: The Lee Resolution contained three parts: a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances

overview.headline: Lee resolution proposed independence and shaped founding actions

keyPoints.point: Richard Henry Lee introduced resolution proposing independence in Congress
keyPoints.quote: Richard Henry Lee of Virginia, introduced this resolution in the Second Continental Congress proposing independence

keyPoints.point: Many colonists began seriously considering cutting ties with Britain after fighting started
keyPoints.quote: For the first time, many colonists began to seriously consider cutting ties with Britain.

keyPoints.point: Resolution had three parts covering declaration independence alliances and confederation
keyPoints.quote: a declaration of independence, a call to form foreign alliances, and "a plan for confederation."

keyPoints.point: Congress deferred approval then adopted first part declaration
keyPoints.quote: approval was deferred until July 2. On that date, Congress adopted the first part (the declaration).

keyTerms.gloss: group of elected delegates that became governing body during Revolution
keyTerms.quote: The colonists elected delegates to attend a Continental Congress that eventually became the governing body

keyTerms.gloss: formal statement drafted to proclaim independence from Britain
keyTerms.quote: one to draft a declaration of independence, a second to draw up a plan

keyTerms.gloss: agreements forming partnerships with foreign nations for support
keyTerms.quote: a second to draw up a plan "for forming foreign alliances,"

keyTerms.gloss: plan for uniting colonies under shared confederation agreement

analysis.pageCoverage: Page covers colonial move toward independence, Lee resolution with declaration alliances and confederation, committee work, vote and later approvals
